knowledge:
- key_parameters: eset=An ExpressionSet containing normalized intensity values on a raw scale (positive, not logarithmic) ;; sampleLabels=A vector or phenoData column name indicating the class of each sample (balanced sample sizes per class are highly recommended) ;; estimateGError=Logical indicating whether to estimate the generalization error using nested cross-validation (default FALSE) ;; skipInteractions=Logical to skip mutual information calculations to speed up execution (default FALSE) ;; lpThreshold=Posterior probability threshold to define significant genes (default 0.95) ;; geneLabels=Optional data frame or vector mapping gene IDs to readable symbols ;; minProbAssignCoeff=Coefficient determining the minimum probability required to assign a sample to a class (default 1) ;; minDiffAssignCoeff=Coefficient determining the minimum probability difference between the first and second most likely classes to assign a sample (default 0.8)
- alternatives: EBarrays (specifically the emfit function) is used internally for Parametric Empirical Bayes gene ranking ;; minet is used internally for mutual information network calculations ;; e1071 is used internally for multi-class SVM classification ;; GATExplorer annotation files are recommended for mapping Ensembl IDs to Gene Symbols when using GATExplorer custom CDFs
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have genome-wide gene expression data across multiple biological states or disease subtypes and want to identify class-specific gene signatures, build a multi-class SVM classifier, predict the class of new samples with a "NotAssigned" option for low-certainty cases, and construct co-expression networks for each class.
- pitfalls: Input expression data must be normalized intensity values on a raw scale (positive and not log-transformed) because the underlying EBarrays package requires raw-scale data ;; Unbalanced sample sizes across classes can bias the classifier training and evaluation ;; Setting estimateGError=TRUE significantly increases execution time due to nested cross-validation loops ;; If the input features are probesets rather than summarized genes, the package will still run but will refer to them as "genes" in the outputs and plots

workflows.name: train_classifier_and_networks
workflows.intent: Train a multi-class SVM classifier, rank significant genes, estimate generalization error, and construct co-expression networks from gene expression data.
input: expression_data.RData (ExpressionSet containing normalized raw-scale gene expression values)
sample_metadata.csv (metadata containing class labels for each sample)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the gene expression dataset and define training samples.
2. Run geNetClassifier() to rank genes, train the SVM classifier, estimate generalization error, and build co-expression networks.
3. Inspect the ranked genes and significant gene counts using getRanking(), getTopRanking(), and genesDetails().
4. Evaluate classifier performance and generalization error using the confusion matrix and probability matrix.
5. Export the constructed gene networks to text files for external visualization.
workflows.code:
library(geNetClassifier)
library(leukemiasEset)
data(leukemiasEset)
trainSamples <- c(1:10, 13:22, 25:34, 37:46, 49:58)
data(geneSymbols)
leukemiasClassifier <- geNetClassifier(eset=leukemiasEset[,trainSamples], sampleLabels="LeukemiaType", plotsName="leukemiasClassifier", estimateGError=TRUE, geneLabels=geneSymbols)
names(leukemiasClassifier)
leukemiasClassifier@genesRanking
numGenes(leukemiasClassifier@genesRanking)
subRanking <- getTopRanking(leukemiasClassifier@genesRanking, 10)
getRanking(subRanking)
getRanking(subRanking, showGeneID=TRUE)$geneID[,1:4]
genesDetails(subRanking)$AML
numSignificantGenes(leukemiasClassifier@genesRanking)
leukemiasClassifier@classifier
leukemiasClassifier@classificationGenes
leukemiasClassifier@generalizationError
leukemiasClassifier@generalizationError@confMatrix
leukemiasClassifier@generalizationError@probMatrix
leukemiasClassifier@genesNetwork
network2txt(leukemiasClassifier@genesNetwork, filePrefix="leukemiasNetwork")

workflows.name: query_new_samples
workflows.intent: Classify new independent samples of known or unknown class using a pre-trained geNetClassifier model and evaluate prediction accuracy.
input: query_expression_data.RData (ExpressionSet containing normalized raw-scale gene expression values for new samples)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the pre-trained classifier and the query expression dataset.
2. Run queryGeNetClassifier() to predict classes and calculate assignment probabilities for the new samples.
3. Perform external validation by generating a confusion matrix and calculating validation statistics.
4. Adjust assignment stringency thresholds (minProbAssignCoeff and minDiffAssignCoeff) to control "NotAssigned" calls.
5. Summarize the query results.
workflows.code:
library(geNetClassifier)
library(leukemiasEset)
data(leukemiasEset)
data(leukemiasClassifier)
testSamples <- c(1:60)[-trainSamples]
queryResult <- queryGeNetClassifier(leukemiasClassifier, leukemiasEset[,testSamples])
queryResult$class
queryResult$probabilities
confusionMatrix <- table(leukemiasEset[,testSamples]$LeukemiaType, queryResult$class)
externalValidation.stats(confusionMatrix)
externalValidation.probMatrix(queryResult, leukemiasEset[,testSamples]$LeukemiaType, numDecimals=3)
queryResult_AssignAll <- queryGeNetClassifier(leukemiasClassifier, leukemiasEset[,testSamples], minProbAssignCoeff=0, minDiffAssignCoeff=0)
queryResult_AssignLess <- queryGeNetClassifier(leukemiasClassifier, leukemiasEset[,testSamples], minProbAssignCoeff=1.5, minDiffAssignCoeff=1)
querySummary(queryResult, numDecimals=3)

workflows.name: visualize_classifier_results
workflows.intent: Generate diagnostic and biological plots including ranked significant genes, gene expression profiles, discriminant power, and gene networks.
input: expression_data.RData (ExpressionSet containing normalized raw-scale gene expression values)
workflows.stages:
1. Plot the posterior probabilities of ranked genes to visualize the significance threshold.
2. Plot gene expression profiles across samples as line plots or boxplots.
3. Plot the discriminant power of key classification genes.
4. Extract and plot class-specific gene sub-networks.
workflows.code:
library(geNetClassifier)
library(leukemiasEset)
data(leukemiasEset)
data(leukemiasClassifier)
data(geneSymbols)
plot(leukemiasClassifier@genesRanking)
plot(leukemiasClassifier@genesRanking, numGenesPlot=3000, lpThreshold=0.80)
topGenes <- getRanking(getTopRanking(leukemiasClassifier@classificationGenes,numGenesClass=1), showGeneID=TRUE)$geneID
plotExpressionProfiles(leukemiasEset, topGenes[,c("ALL","AML"), drop=FALSE], sampleLabels="LeukemiaType", geneLabels=geneSymbols)
plotExpressionProfiles(leukemiasEset[,trainSamples], leukemiasClassifier, sampleLabels="LeukemiaType", fileName="leukExprs_trainSamples.pdf")
plotDiscriminantPower(leukemiasClassifier, classificationGenes="ENSG00000169575")
discPowerTable <- plotDiscriminantPower(leukemiasClassifier, classificationGenes=getRanking(leukemiasClassifier@classificationGenes, showGeneID=TRUE)$geneID[1:4,"AML",drop=FALSE], returnTable=TRUE)
clGenesSubNet <- getSubNetwork(leukemiasClassifier@genesNetwork, leukemiasClassifier@classificationGenes)
clGenesInfo <- genesDetails(leukemiasClassifier@classificationGenes)
plotNetwork(genesNetwork=clGenesSubNet$ALL, genesInfo=clGenesInfo)
